definitions.explanation: Describing coffee, tea, or other beverages that have just been prepared.

examples.japanese: {淹|い}れ{立|た}てのコーヒーを{飲|の}む。
{淹|い}れ{立|た}ての{紅茶|こうちゃ}は{香|かお}りがいい。
examples.english: Freshly brewed tea has a nice aroma.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{淹|い}れ{立|た}てのコーヒーで{一日|いちにち}を{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: Every morning, I start the day with freshly brewed coffee.

notes:
{淹|い}れ{立|た}て is part of a common pattern using ～{立|た}て to indicate something just done.

FORMS:
- {淹|い}れる (to brew) + {立|た}て (just done)

SIMILAR ～{立|た}て PATTERNS:
- {焼|や}き{立|た}て: freshly baked
- {揚|あ}げ{立|た}て: freshly fried
- {出来立|できた}て: freshly made
- {炊|た}き{立|た}て: freshly cooked (rice)

SPELLING NOTE:
- Also written as {入|い}れ{立|た}て using a simpler kanji
- Often written in hiragana as いれたて

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {淹|い}れ{立|た}てのコーヒー: freshly brewed coffee
- {淹|い}れ{立|た}ての{緑茶|りょくちゃ}: freshly made green tea
